**Group:** Zooplankton  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A phaeodarian (Phaeodaria): a large single-celled marine protist (Rhizaria) with a hollow, porous skeleton of silica and organic material — often geometric, latticed, or bearing hollow spines — and a distinctive phaeodium, a dense mass of dark greenish-brown pigmented particles sitting beside the central capsule near its main aperture (astropyle). Key features: hollow/porous silica skeleton plus the conspicuous dark phaeodium. Note: a protist grouped here with the larger heterotrophs.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **acantharia** | Acantharia have solid radial strontium-sulfate spines and no phaeodium; phaeodarians have a hollow porous silica skeleton and a conspicuous dark phaeodium. |
| **aggregate** | The dark phaeodium can resemble detritus, but a phaeodarian shows an organised skeleton and central capsule; aggregates are unstructured flocs. |
